editorial.meta_description: CompTIA Linux+ XK0-005 retired on 2026-01-13. Review exam details and transition to its replacement path, XK0-006.
editorial.overview: The CompTIA Linux+ certification covers multiple topics associated with Linux systems. Retired as of 2026-01-13, the evaluation was structured around four distinct domains including System Management, Security, Scripting Containers and Automation, and Troubleshooting. CompTIA has designated XK0-006 as the replacement exam code for candidates seeking this certification path under current registry guidelines. The exam featured a total of 90 questions administered over a duration of 90 minutes to test candidate proficiency.
editorial.who_should_take: This certification exam is intended for IT professionals working with Linux systems who need to demonstrate operational knowledge across management, security, scripting, and troubleshooting domains.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Candidates preparing for this assessment should review the published exam objectives carefully and study official documentation such as system manual pages and configuration guides. It is exceptionally useful to practice command-line operations, file permissions, and process management to ensure adequate preparation for all topics covered.

faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?
faq.answer_text: The exam consists of a total of 90 questions. The question formats include multiple choice with single answers, multiple choice with multiple answers, and performance-based items administered during the test.
The passing score for the exam is set at 720 on a scale of 100 to 900. Candidates must meet or exceed this score to pass the assessment successfully.
The total test duration is exactly 90 minutes. Candidates must complete all exam questions within this allocated timeframe according to the published guidelines established by CompTIA.
The official exam price is established at USD 369.0. Please note that since the exam is retired, registration is no longer active for this specific code.
